```{r unvalidated IDs}

# 1. Set the path to your main umbrella directory
# main_directory <- here('SSL Perinatal Project', 'data')

# 2. Recursively find every .xlsx file in all subfolders
# excel_files <- dir_ls(main_directory, recurse = TRUE, glob = "*.xlsx")
excel_files <- dir_ls(here('data'), recurse = T, glob = '*.xlsx')

# 3. Read them all and bind them together
combined_data <- excel_files %>% 
  # map_df loops through each file path, reads it, and stacks them up.
  # .id = "source_file" creates a brand-new column containing the file path!
  map_df(~ read_excel(.x), .id = "source_file") %>% 
  mutate(date = make_date(year, month, day)) %>%
  dplyr::rename(AnimalID = animalid, SiteName = sitename, Year = year, Behavior = behavior) %>%
  dplyr::select(brand, AnimalID, SiteName, Year, date, Behavior)

unread_IDs <- combined_data %>% dplyr::select(brand, AnimalID) %>% distinct() %>% filter(!is.na(AnimalID))

dat <- combined_data %>% 
  merge(unread_IDs %>% dplyr::rename(ID_missing = AnimalID), by = (c('brand'))) %>%
  mutate(AnimalID_corr = coalesce(AnimalID, ID_missing)) %>%
  dplyr::select(-c(ID_missing, AnimalID)) %>%
  rename(AnimalID = AnimalID_corr)

```

```{r tidy model data}
# 1. STANDARDIZE EVENT CODES FOR MULTIEVENT MODEL

# State-based Event Mapping (c):
# 0 = Not Detected / No Camera Effort in that hour
# 1 = Detected on land, NO PUP or UNKNOWN/AMBIGUOUS PUP STATUS
# 2 = Detected on land, Confirmed WITH Pup (NP, NPJ, WP, WPJ)

obs_clean <- res_remote %>%
  mutate(
    Region = ifelse(grepl('UGAMAK', SiteName), "E ALEU", 'C/W ALEU'),
    # Ensure correct POSIXct format for 1-hour binning
    ts = if ("timestamp" %in% names(.)) {
      timestamp
    } else {
      as.POSIXct(date, tz = "UTC")
    },
    
    # Floor timestamps to 1-hour resolution
    # time_bin = floor_date(ts, unit = "1 hour"),
    time_bin = floor_date(ts, unit = "6 hours"),
    
    # Hierarchical event assignment for individual photo frames:
    # Priority: Confirmed Pup (2) > Detected on land with No Pup/Unknown (1)
    event_code_raw = case_when(
      Behavior %in% pup_yes ~ 2,
      TRUE                  ~ 1  # Female detected, but No Pup or Unknown
    )
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(time_bin), !is.na(AnimalID))



# 2. AGGREGATE TO 1-HOUR BINS & IDENTIFY INITIAL BIRTH WINDOWS

obs_1hr <- obs_clean %>%
  group_by(AnimalID, year, time_bin, Region) %>%
  summarise(
    # Pick highest certainty event code if multiple photos occur within the hour
    # If ANY photo in that hour has a verified pup, code = 2; otherwise code = 1
    event_code = case_when(
      any(event_code_raw == 2) ~ 2,
      TRUE                     ~ 1
    ),
    n_photos = n(), # Sampling effort covariate
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

# Calculate initial birth timestamp (t0) per female-year
female_birth_t0 <- obs_1hr %>%
  filter(event_code == 2) %>%
  group_by(AnimalID, year, Region) %>%
  summarise(
    t0_birth = min(time_bin),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )


# 3. CONSTRUCT PERINATAL TIME GRID (-48h pre-birth to +22d post-birth)

# Setting the post-birth window to 22 days (576 hours total) ensures all long-fasting females in E ALEU and C/W ALEU are fully captured

grid_perinatal_1hr <- female_birth_t0 %>%
  group_by(AnimalID, year, Region) %>%
  reframe(
    time_bin = seq(
      from = t0_birth - hours(48),   # 48 hours pre-first pup sighting
      to   = t0_birth + days(22),     # 22 days post-first pup sighting
      by   = "1 hour"
    )
  ) %>%
  group_by(AnimalID, year, Region) %>%
  mutate(hour_step = row_number()) %>%
  ungroup()


# 4. JOIN GRID & BUILD HMM CAPTURE HISTORIES

ch_perinatal_long <- grid_perinatal_1hr %>%
  left_join(obs_1hr, by = c("AnimalID", "year", "time_bin", 'Region')) %>%
  mutate(
    event_code = replace_na(event_code, 0), # 0 = Not seen / At Sea
    n_photos   = replace_na(n_photos, 0),   # Camera offline / zero photos
    ind_year   = paste(AnimalID, year, sep = "_")
  )

# Extract Format for 'marked' or HMM Likelihood Maximization
# Long-format character histories (ch)
ch_marked_format <- ch_perinatal_long %>%
  group_by(ind_year, AnimalID, year, Region) %>%
  summarise(
    ch = paste0(event_code, collapse = ""),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  left_join(inits %>% select(AnimalID, SiteName), by = "AnimalID")

# Observation Matrix (Rows = Female-Year, Columns = Hour_1..576)
y_matrix_perinatal <- ch_perinatal_long %>%
  select(ind_year, hour_step, event_code) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = hour_step, 
    names_prefix = "h_", 
    values_from = event_code
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("ind_year") %>%
  as.matrix()

# Effort / Photo Count Matrix (Covariate Matrix)
effort_matrix_perinatal <- ch_perinatal_long %>%
  select(ind_year, hour_step, n_photos) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = hour_step, 
    names_prefix = "h_", 
    values_from = n_photos
  ) %>%
  column_to_rownames("ind_year") %>%
  as.matrix()

```

```{r mod1 code}

##time-constant p(leave)
#check whether p(missing female) same between CW ALEU AND E ALEU

library(nimble)

#states:
## 1: perinatal, on land
## 2: first foraging trip, at sea
## 3: on land

hmm_code <- nimbleCode({
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # A. PRIORS 
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  # 1. State Transition Priors
  for (r in 1:n_regions) {
    # hourly probability of leaving perinatal state (State 1 -> State 2)
    # Prior: Beta(1, 150) implies ~ 0.006 probability per hour, 
    # which roughly centers prior belief at ~7 days (168 hrs) perinatal length.
    phi_depart[r] ~ dbeta(1, 150) 
    
    # Derived quantity: Mean perinatal duration in DAYS
    mean_peri_days[r] <- (1 / phi_depart[r]) / 24
  }
  
  # hourly probability of returning from 1st trip (State 2 -> State 3)
  # Beta(1, 50) roughly implies a 2-day first foraging trip
  phi_return ~ dbeta(1, 50)
  
  # Normal post-perinatal cycling (States 3 <-> 4)
  phi_cycle_depart ~ dbeta(1, 50)
  phi_cycle_return ~ dbeta(1, 50)
  
  # 2. Observation / Detection Priors
  # Prob of detecting female on land per hour (if she is present)
  # Beta(7, 3) centers prior at ~70% hourly detection rate
  p_land ~ dbeta(7, 3) 
  
  # Prob of confirming pup IF female is detected
  # High probability during perinatal (e.g., 80%)
  r_pup_peri ~ dbeta(8, 2)
  # Lower probability post-perinatal when pup is older/stashed (e.g., 20%)
  r_pup_post ~ dbeta(2, 8)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # B. STATE TRANSITION MATRIX (Gamma)
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # Dimensions: Gamma[region, current_state, next_state]
  for (r in 1:n_regions) {
    # State 1: Perinatal Land -> can stay(1) or depart(2)
    Gamma[r, 1, 1] <- 1 - phi_depart[r]
    Gamma[r, 1, 2] <- phi_depart[r]
    Gamma[r, 1, 3] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 1, 4] <- 0
    
    # State 2: First Foraging Trip (Sea) -> can stay(2) or return(3)
    Gamma[r, 2, 1] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 2, 2] <- 1 - phi_return
    Gamma[r, 2, 3] <- phi_return
    Gamma[r, 2, 4] <- 0
    
    # State 3: Post-trip Land -> can stay(3) or depart(4)
    Gamma[r, 3, 1] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 3, 2] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 3, 3] <- 1 - phi_cycle_depart
    Gamma[r, 3, 4] <- phi_cycle_depart
    
    # State 4: Post-trip Sea -> can stay(4) or return(3)
    Gamma[r, 4, 1] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 4, 2] <- 0
    Gamma[r, 4, 3] <- phi_cycle_return
    Gamma[r, 4, 4] <- 1 - phi_cycle_return
  }
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # C. OBSERVATION MATRIX (Omega)
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # Dimensions: Omega[true_state, observed_state]
  
  # State 1: Perinatal Land
  Omega[1, 1] <- 1 - p_land                    # Not seen
  Omega[1, 2] <- p_land * (1 - r_pup_peri)     # Seen, no pup
  Omega[1, 3] <- p_land * r_pup_peri           # Seen, with pup
  
  # State 2: First Trip Sea (Cannot be seen)
  Omega[2, 1] <- 1
  Omega[2, 2] <- 0
  Omega[2, 3] <- 0
  
  # State 3: Post-trip Land
  Omega[3, 1] <- 1 - p_land
  Omega[3, 2] <- p_land * (1 - r_pup_post)
  Omega[3, 3] <- p_land * r_pup_post
  
  # State 4: Post-trip Sea (Cannot be seen)
  Omega[4, 1] <- 1
  Omega[4, 2] <- 0
  Omega[4, 3] <- 0

  # -------------------------------------------------
  # D. LIKELIHOOD
  # -------------------------------------------------
  for (i in 1:N) {
    # Initialize true state at t0 (which is hour 49 in your matrix)
    z[i, t0_idx] <- 1 
    
    # Model forward from t0+1 to the end of the 22 days
    for (t in (t0_idx + 1):T_max) {
      
      # 1. State process: what state is she in at time t?
      z[i, t] ~ dcat(Gamma[region[i], z[i, t-1], 1:4])
      
      # 2. Observation process: what do we see at time t?
      y[i, t] ~ dcat(Omega[z[i, t], 1:3])
    }
  }
})


#run model
# 1. Shift observations so 0s become 1s (NIMBLE needs 1, 2, 3)
y_nimble <- y_matrix_perinatal + 1 

# 2. Extract covariates based on row order of the matrix
# Ensure the order matches row.names(y_matrix_perinatal)
covs <- ch_perinatal_long %>%
  dplyr::select(ind_year, AnimalID, Region) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(match(ind_year, rownames(y_matrix_perinatal)))

# Convert region to numeric index (e.g., 1 = E ALEU, 2 = C/W ALEU)
region_idx <- as.numeric(as.factor(covs$Region))

# 3. Create Data and Constants lists
nimble_consts <- list(
  N = nrow(y_nimble),
  T_max = ncol(y_nimble),  # should be 576 + 48 = 624
  t0_idx = 49,             # hour_step where birth was confirmed
  n_regions = max(region_idx),
  region = region_idx
)

nimble_data <- list(
  y = y_nimble
)

# Smart initialization for Z matrix
z_init <- matrix(NA, nrow = nimble_consts$N, ncol = nimble_consts$T_max)
for (i in 1:nimble_consts$N) {
  # Everything after t0 starts in state 1 (Perinatal Land)
  z_init[i, (nimble_consts$t0_idx + 1):nimble_consts$T_max] <- 1 
}

nimble_inits <- list(
  phi_depart = rep(0.005, nimble_consts$n_regions),
  phi_return = 0.02,
  phi_cycle_depart = 0.02,
  phi_cycle_return = 0.02,
  p_land = 0.7,
  r_pup_peri = 0.8,
  r_pup_post = 0.2,
  z = z_init
)

# Build, Compile, and Run
model <- nimbleModel(code = hmm_code, constants = nimble_consts, 
                     data = nimble_data, inits = nimble_inits)
cModel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors = c("mean_peri_days", "phi_depart", "p_land", "r_pup_peri"))
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cMCMC <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = model)

# Run a quick proof-of-concept chain
samples <- runMCMC(cMCMC, niter = 5000, nburnin = 1000, thin = 1, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)
plot(samples)


```


```{r mod2 code}

##time-varying p(leave); hazard function

library(nimble)

#states:
## 1: perinatal, on land
## 2: first foraging trip, at sea
## 3: on land

hmm_code <- nimbleCode({
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # A. PRIORS 
  # -------------------------------------------------
  
  # 1. State Transition Priors
  for (r in 1:n_regions) {
    # 1. Weibull Shape Parameter (k)
    # k = 1 is a constant hazard (exponential). 
    # k > 1 means the probability of leaving INCREASES as time goes on (target departure day).
    # k < 1 means the probability decreases (highly unlikely for sea lions).
    shape[r] ~ dunif(1, 10) 
    
    # 2. Weibull Scale Parameter (lambda) - in HOURS
    # This dictates the overall duration. If expected duration is ~7 days, 
    # the scale will be around 168 hours.
    scale[r] ~ dunif(1, 1000) 
    
    # Derived quantity: Median perinatal duration in DAYS
    # Median of Weibull = scale * (ln(2))^(1/shape)
    median_peri_days[r] <- (scale[r] * (log(2))^(1/shape[r])) / 24
    
  }
  
  # Constant nuisance parameters for states 2, 3, and 4
  phi_return ~ dbeta(1, 50)
  phi_cycle_depart <- phi_cycle_depart_fixed  # Passed in as a constant to save MCMC time and recognize that we care less about it
  phi_cycle_return <- phi_cycle_return_fixed
  
  # 2. Observation / Detection Priors
  # Prob of detecting female on land per hour (if she is present)
  # Beta(7, 3) centers prior at ~70% hourly detection rate
  p_land ~ dbeta(7, 3) 
  
  # Prob of confirming pup IF female is detected
  # High probability during perinatal (e.g., 80%)
  r_pup_peri ~ dbeta(8, 2)
  # Lower probability post-perinatal when pup is older/stashed (e.g., 20%)
  r_pup_post ~ dbeta(2, 8)
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # B. STATE TRANSITION MATRIX (Gamma)
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # Dimensions: Gamma[region, current_state, next_state]
  for (r in 1:n_regions) {
    
    # We only calculate the hazard AFTER birth (t0_idx)
    for (t in (t0_idx + 1):T_max) {
      
      # tau is "hours since birth"
      tau[t] <- t - t0_idx
      
      # Discrete Weibull Hazard: Probability of leaving in this specific hour
      phi_depart[r, t] <- 1 - exp( ((tau[t] - 1) / scale[r])^shape[r] - 
                                   (tau[t] / scale[r])^shape[r] )
      
      # State 1: Perinatal Land -> can stay(1) or depart(2)
      Gamma[r, t, 1, 1] <- 1 - phi_depart[r, t]
      Gamma[r, t, 1, 2] <- phi_depart[r, t]
      Gamma[r, t, 1, 3] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 1, 4] <- 0
      
      # State 2: First Foraging Trip (Sea) -> can stay(2) or return(3)
      Gamma[r, t, 2, 1] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 2, 2] <- 1 - phi_return
      Gamma[r, t, 2, 3] <- phi_return
      Gamma[r, t, 2, 4] <- 0
      
      # State 3: Post-trip Land -> can stay(3) or depart(4)
      Gamma[r, t, 3, 1] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 3, 2] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 3, 3] <- 1 - phi_cycle_depart
      Gamma[r, t, 3, 4] <- phi_cycle_depart
      
      # State 4: Post-trip Sea -> can stay(4) or return(3)
      Gamma[r, t, 4, 1] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 4, 2] <- 0
      Gamma[r, t, 4, 3] <- phi_cycle_return
      Gamma[r, t, 4, 4] <- 1 - phi_cycle_return
    }
  }
  
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # C. OBSERVATION MATRIX (Omega)
  # -------------------------------------------------
  # Dimensions: Omega[true_state, observed_state]
  
  # State 1: Perinatal Land
  Omega[1, 1] <- 1 - p_land                    # Not seen
  Omega[1, 2] <- p_land * (1 - r_pup_peri)     # Seen, no pup
  Omega[1, 3] <- p_land * r_pup_peri           # Seen, with pup
  
  # State 2: First Trip Sea (Cannot be seen)
  Omega[2, 1] <- 1
  Omega[2, 2] <- 0
  Omega[2, 3] <- 0
  
  # State 3: Post-trip Land
  Omega[3, 1] <- 1 - p_land
  Omega[3, 2] <- p_land * (1 - r_pup_post)
  Omega[3, 3] <- p_land * r_pup_post
  
  # State 4: Post-trip Sea (Cannot be seen)
  Omega[4, 1] <- 1
  Omega[4, 2] <- 0
  Omega[4, 3] <- 0

  # -------------------------------------------------
  # D. LIKELIHOOD
  # -------------------------------------------------
  for (i in 1:N) {
    # Initialize true state at t0 (which is hour 49 in your matrix)
    z[i, t0_idx] <- 1 
    
    # Model forward from t0+1 to the end of the 22 days
    for (t in (t0_idx + 1):T_max) {
      
      # 1. State process: what state is she in at time t?
      z[i, t] ~ dcat(Gamma[region[i], t, z[i, t-1], 1:4])
      
      # 2. Observation process: what do we see at time t?
      y[i, t] ~ dcat(Omega[z[i, t], 1:3])
    }
  }
})


#run model
# 1. Shift observations so 0s become 1s (NIMBLE needs 1, 2, 3)
y_nimble <- y_matrix_perinatal + 1 

# 2. Extract covariates based on row order of the matrix
# Ensure the order matches row.names(y_matrix_perinatal)
covs <- ch_perinatal_long %>%
  select(ind_year, AnimalID, Region) %>%
  distinct() %>%
  arrange(match(ind_year, rownames(y_matrix_perinatal)))

# Convert region to numeric index (e.g., 1 = E ALEU, 2 = C/W ALEU)
region_idx <- as.numeric(as.factor(covs$Region))

# 3. Create Data and Constants lists
nimble_consts <- list(
  N = nrow(y_nimble),
  T_max = ncol(y_nimble),  # should be 576 + 48 = 624
  t0_idx = 49,             # hour_step where birth was confirmed
  n_regions = max(region_idx),
  region = region_idx
)

nimble_data <- list(
  y = y_nimble
)

# Smart initialization for Z matrix
z_init <- matrix(NA, nrow = nimble_consts$N, ncol = nimble_consts$T_max)
for (i in 1:nimble_consts$N) {
  # Everything after t0 starts in state 1 (Perinatal Land)
  z_init[i, (nimble_consts$t0_idx + 1):nimble_consts$T_max] <- 1 
}

nimble_inits <- list(
  phi_depart = rep(0.005, nimble_consts$n_regions),
  phi_return = 0.02,
  phi_cycle_depart = 0.02,
  phi_cycle_return = 0.02,
  p_land = 0.7,
  r_pup_peri = 0.8,
  r_pup_post = 0.2,
  z = z_init
)

# Build, Compile, and Run
model <- nimbleModel(code = hmm_code, constants = nimble_consts, 
                     data = nimble_data, inits = nimble_inits)
cModel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors = c("mean_peri_days", "phi_depart", "p_land", "r_pup_peri"))
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cMCMC <- compileNimble(mcmc, project = model)

# Run a quick proof-of-concept chain
samples <- runMCMC(cMCMC, niter = 5000, nburnin = 1000, thin = 1, samplesAsCodaMCMC = TRUE)
plot(samples)
```

```{r figures}
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Convert the MCMC matrix into a tidy dataframe
# If you ran multiple chains, you might need: post_df <- as.data.frame(do.call(rbind, samples))
post_df <- as.data.frame(samples) %>%
  # Select the derived perinatal length parameters
  select(`median_peri_days[1]`, `median_peri_days[2]`) %>%
  # Rename to match your regions (assuming 1 = E ALEU, 2 = C/W ALEU)
  rename(
    `E ALEU` = `median_peri_days[1]`,
    `C/W ALEU` = `median_peri_days[2]`
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(), 
    names_to = "Region", 
    values_to = "Perinatal_Days"
  )

# 2. Create the overlapping density plot
ggplot(post_df, aes(x = Perinatal_Days, fill = Region)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.6, color = "black", linewidth = 0.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("E ALEU" = "#E69F00", "C/W ALEU" = "#56B4E9")) +
  labs(
    title = "Posterior Estimate of Median Perinatal Length",
    subtitle = "Accounting for imperfect detection and pup visibility",
    x = "Median Perinatal Duration (Days)",
    y = "Posterior Density",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )

##visualizing Weibull curve
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Define the time sequence to predict over
day_seq <- seq(0, 14, by = 0.1)
hour_seq <- day_seq * 24

# 2. Extract full posterior chains for the shape and scale parameters
shape1 <- samples[, "shape[1]"]
scale1 <- samples[, "scale[1]"]
shape2 <- samples[, "shape[2]"]
scale2 <- samples[, "scale[2]"]

# 3. Calculate the curve for EVERY iteration (Rows = iterations, Cols = time steps)
# Multiplying by 24 scales the hourly density up to a daily density
dens_matrix_1 <- sapply(hour_seq, function(h) {
  dweibull(h, shape = shape1, scale = scale1) * 24
})

dens_matrix_2 <- sapply(hour_seq, function(h) {
  dweibull(h, shape = shape2, scale = scale2) * 24
})

# 4. Extract the 2.5%, 50% (median), and 97.5% quantiles at each time step
ci_1 <- apply(dens_matrix_1, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)
ci_2 <- apply(dens_matrix_2, 2, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.5, 0.975), na.rm = TRUE)

# 5. Package into a tidy dataframe for ggplot
ci_data <- bind_rows(
  tibble(
    day = day_seq,
    median = ci_1[2, ],
    lwr = ci_1[1, ],
    upr = ci_1[3, ],
    Region = "E ALEU"
  ),
  tibble(
    day = day_seq,
    median = ci_2[2, ],
    lwr = ci_2[1, ],
    upr = ci_2[3, ],
    Region = "C/W ALEU"
  )
)

# 6. Plot the curves with 95% Credible Interval ribbons
ggplot(ci_data, aes(x = day, fill = Region, color = Region)) +
  # The 95% CI ribbon (alpha makes it semi-transparent so overlaps are visible)
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr, ymax = upr), alpha = 0.3, color = NA) +
  # The median prediction line
  geom_line(aes(y = median), linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("E ALEU" = "#E69F00", "C/W ALEU" = "#56B4E9")) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("E ALEU" = "#E69F00", "C/W ALEU" = "#56B4E9")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 14, by = 2)) +
  labs(
    title = "Timing of First Foraging Trip with 95% Credible Intervals",
    subtitle = "Probability of departure occurring on a given day post-birth",
    x = "Days Since Birth",
    y = "Probability Density",
    color = "Region",
    fill = "Region"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
